description: Experience the true taste of Liguria with our authentic Focaccia Genovese, a beloved Italian flatbread. This recipe guides you to create a perfectly airy, chewy, and crispy focaccia, generously infused with fragrant rosemary and high-quality olive oil. It is an ideal accompaniment to any meal or a delightful snack on its own.

ingredients.notes: Plus extra for drizzling and pan

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough Base
instructions.text: In a large bowl, dissolve the fresh yeast in lukewarm water. If using active dry yeast, let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. Add the strong bread flour and fine sea salt, mixing with a wooden spoon or by hand until a shaggy dough forms. Gradually add 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil.

instructions.title: Knead and Develop Gluten
instructions.text: Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface and knead for about 10-15 minutes until it becomes smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. Alternatively, use a stand mixer with a dough hook for 8-10 minutes on medium speed. The dough should be soft but manageable.

instructions.title: First Proofing
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until it has doubled in size. This is the first proof.

instructions.title: Prepare and Dimple the Focaccia
instructions.text: Generously oil a 30x40 cm (12x16 inch) baking tray with extra virgin olive oil. Gently transfer the risen dough to the tray, stretching it carefully to fill the pan. Cover again and let it rest for another 30 minutes. After resting, use your fingertips to create deep dimples all over the surface of the dough.

instructions.title: Add Brine, Rosemary, and Salt
instructions.text: In a small bowl, whisk together 4 tablespoons of lukewarm water and 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil to create an emulsion (brine). Pour this mixture evenly over the dimpled focaccia. Sprinkle the picked fresh rosemary leaves and coarse sea salt over the entire surface.

instructions.title: Final Proof and Bake
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 220C (425F). Let the focaccia rest for a final 15-20 minutes while the oven preheats. Bake for 25-35 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and cooked through. The bottom should also be nicely browned.

instructions.title: Serve with a Drizzle of Olive Oil
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the focaccia from the oven. For an authentic touch, immediately drizzle a little more high-quality extra virgin olive oil over the hot focaccia. Let it cool slightly on a wire rack before slicing and serving. Enjoy warm or at room temperature.

tips: For the best texture, ensure your water is lukewarm (not hot) to activate the yeast without killing it. A kitchen thermometer is your friend.
Use a high-quality extra virgin olive oil, especially for the final drizzle. It makes a significant difference in the flavor profile of authentic Focaccia Genovese.
Focaccia is best enjoyed fresh on the day it's baked. If you have leftovers, lightly toast them to revive their crispiness.
article:
Focaccia Genovese, a culinary jewel from the sun-drenched region of Liguria, Italy, is far more than just flatbread. It's a testament to the power of simple, high-quality ingredients transformed into something extraordinary. Imagine a golden, dimpled surface glistening with olive oil, a delicate crunch giving way to an impossibly soft, airy crumb, all infused with the aromatic embrace of fresh rosemary. This isn't just bread; it's an experience, a slice of Italian tradition that evokes seaside breezes and rustic charm. If you've ever dreamt of recreating the magic of a Ligurian bakery in your own kitchen, diving into a Focaccia Genovese recipe is an absolute must. It’s an Italian baking adventure that promises immense satisfaction and incredible flavor.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?
At its heart, Focaccia Genovese is the quintessential Ligurian focaccia, distinct from its counterparts across Italy. Originating in Genoa, the capital of Liguria, this particular focaccia is renowned for its unique texture and preparation. Unlike thicker, bread-like focaccias found elsewhere, the Genovese version is characteristically thinner, boasts a remarkably soft and airy interior, and a deliciously crisp bottom crust. Its signature feature is the generous application of extra virgin olive oil, both in the dough and drizzled generously over the surface before baking, creating those iconic dimples that pool with golden goodness. Another defining characteristic is the brine or emulsion of water, salt, and olive oil that is poured over the dough before its final proof and bake, contributing to its distinct texture and irresistible flavor profile. It's often called "a schiacciata," meaning "flattened," perfectly describing its form. The result is a savory, aromatic flatbread that is both rustic and refined, a staple in Ligurian households and bakeries, enjoyed from breakfast to dinner.

## Ingredients for Authentic Focaccia Genovese
Crafting the perfect Focaccia Genovese recipe begins with selecting the right ingredients. Quality here is paramount, as the simplicity of the recipe allows each component to shine.
-   **Strong Bread Flour (Type 0 or 00):** A high-protein flour is crucial for developing the gluten structure needed to achieve the focaccia's characteristic airy crumb and chewiness.
-   **Fresh Yeast or Active Dry Yeast:** Fresh yeast offers a nuanced flavor, but active dry yeast works perfectly well. Ensure your yeast is fresh and active for a good rise.
-   **Water:** Lukewarm water helps activate the yeast and develop the dough. The hydration level for Focaccia Genovese is typically quite high, contributing to its soft interior.
-   **Fine Sea Salt:** Salt is vital for flavor and for controlling yeast activity. It’s also a key component of the signature brine.
-   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** This is non-negotiable! A high-quality, fruity extra virgin olive oil from Liguria or a similarly excellent region will make all the difference. It’s used in the dough, for oiling the pan, drizzled on top, and as part of the brine. Its flavor is integral to the focaccia's identity.
-   **Fresh Rosemary:** Sprigs of fresh rosemary, roughly chopped, infuse the focaccia with its signature herbaceous aroma and taste. Dried rosemary can be used in a pinch, but fresh is always superior for this dish.

## Step-by-Step: How to Make Focaccia Genovese
Creating this masterpiece is a rewarding process. Follow this Focaccia Genovese recipe for a truly authentic experience.

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the lukewarm water with a pinch of sugar (optional, but helps activate yeast) and the yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until frothy.
2.  **Mix the Dough:** Add the flour and salt to the yeast mixture. Mix with a spoon or your hands until a shaggy, sticky dough forms. This is a high-hydration dough, so don't be tempted to add too much extra flour.
3.  **Initial Kneading (Stretch and Fold):** Drizzle about 2-3 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil over the dough. Using wet hands, perform a series of "stretch and folds" directly in the bowl. Grab a portion of the dough, stretch it upwards, and fold it over itself. Rotate the bowl and repeat this motion 4-5 times. Cover the bowl and let it rest for 15-20 minutes. Repeat this stretch and fold process 3-4 more times, with 15-20 minute rests in between. This gentle kneading develops gluten without extensive effort.
4.  **First Proof (Bulk Fermentation):** After the final stretch and fold, cover the bowl tightly and let the dough rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until it has at least doubled in size.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Generously coat a large rectangular baking pan (approximately 13x18 inches or similar) with extra virgin olive oil.
6.  **Transfer and Dimple:** Gently turn the risen dough out into the prepared pan. Using your oiled fingertips, gently stretch and press the dough to evenly fill the pan. Don't worry if it resists; let it rest for 10 minutes and then continue stretching. Once stretched, use your fingertips to create deep, evenly spaced dimples across the entire surface of the dough.
7.  **Prepare the Brine:** In a small bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup of lukewarm water, 1 teaspoon of fine sea salt, and 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil.
8.  **Second Proof:** Pour the brine evenly over the dimpled dough, ensuring it pools in the indentations. Sprinkle with fresh rosemary. Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel and let it proof again for 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy. Preheat your oven to 450°F (230°C) during the last 15 minutes of proofing.
9.  **Bake:** Place the focaccia in the preheated oven. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and the bottom is crisp and deeply golden.
10. **Cool and Serve:** Once baked, immediately drizzle with a little more extra virgin olive oil. Transfer the focaccia to a wire rack to cool slightly before slicing and serving.

## Tips for Perfect Rosemary Olive Oil Focaccia
Achieving the perfect texture and flavor for your Focaccia Genovese recipe is all about attention to detail.
-   **Embrace High Hydration:** Don't be afraid of sticky dough. The high water content is what gives Focaccia Genovese its characteristic open, airy crumb. Resist the urge to add excessive flour during mixing or handling.
-   **Quality EVOO is Key:** As mentioned, a good quality extra virgin olive oil is non-negotiable. It contributes significantly to the flavor, aroma, and crispy texture.
-   **Gentle Handling:** Treat the dough gently, especially after the first rise. Overworking it will deflate the air bubbles you've worked so hard to create.
-   **Deep Dimples:** Don't be shy with the dimples! These indentations are crucial for catching the olive oil and brine, creating those pockets of flavor and a unique texture.
-   **Proper Proofing:** Allow adequate time for both proofing stages. Under-proofed focaccia will be dense, while over-proofed focaccia might collapse. Look for a visible increase in volume and a puffy texture.
-   **Hot Oven:** A high oven temperature ensures a quick rise and a beautifully crisp crust.
-   **Fresh Rosemary:** While dried herbs have their place, fresh rosemary provides a superior aromatic experience that truly elevates this focaccia.
-   **The Brine:** The salt-water-oil emulsion is a hallmark of Genovese focaccia. It adds moisture, flavor, and helps create the signature bubbly, crisp surface.

## Serving Suggestions for Genovese Focaccia
Once you’ve perfected your Focaccia Genovese recipe, the possibilities for enjoying it are endless.
-   **Standalone Snack:** The simplest and often best way to enjoy it – warm, fresh, and unadorned.
-   **Antipasto Platter:** Serve alongside cured meats like prosciutto or salami, and an assortment of cheeses, olives, and marinated vegetables.
-   **Accompaniment to Meals:** It makes an excellent side for soups, stews, and salads, perfect for soaking up delicious broths and dressings.
-   **Sandwich Bread:** Slice it horizontally and fill with your favorite deli meats, cheeses, roasted vegetables, or a simple caprese.
-   **Dipping:** Serve with a small bowl of high-quality extra virgin olive oil and a dash of balsamic vinegar for dipping.
-   **Breakfast:** In Liguria, it's not uncommon to enjoy a piece of focaccia for breakfast, perhaps even dipped in coffee!

## Variations & Substitutions for Focaccia
While the classic Focaccia Genovese recipe is a masterpiece on its own, don't hesitate to experiment once you've mastered the basic technique.
-   **Toppings:** Beyond rosemary, consider adding cherry tomatoes (pressed into the dimples), thinly sliced red onion, black olives, or even a sprinkle of coarse sea salt flakes for extra crunch.
-   **Herbs:** Experiment with other fresh herbs like thyme or oregano, either alone or in combination with rosemary.
-   **Flour Blends:** While strong bread flour is traditional, you can try substituting a small percentage (up to 20-30%) with whole wheat flour for a nuttier flavor, though this will result in a slightly denser crumb.
-   **Sweet Focaccia:** While less common for the Genovese style, some focaccias are made sweet with sugar, grapes, or honey, but this deviates significantly from the savory rosemary olive oil profile.
-   **Gluten-Free:** For those with sensitivities, gluten-free bread flour blends can be used, but be aware that the texture and rise will differ, and you may need to adjust hydration.

Embrace the journey of making this authentic Focaccia Genovese recipe. It's a culinary experience that connects you to the heart of Italian baking, delivering a taste of Liguria straight to your table. The aroma alone is worth the effort, but the taste of that perfectly crisp, impossibly soft, rosemary-infused bread will keep you coming back for more.
